Short answers up front:
- VAT: Yes, we treat this as a B2B reverse-charge. Our EU VAT registration is FR123456789. Please include Solara's VAT ID on your payment remittance and on the payment reference.
- Fees / routing: we can accept both SHA and OUR, but there are tradeoffs (details below). If Solara prefers a net (no deduction) receipt, please ask your bank to send with OUR so the payer covers all intermediary fees.

Bank details (primary collection account, EUR):
- Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Europe SAS
- Bank: Banque Européenne de Paiement S.A.
- IBAN: FR76 3000 6000 0112 3456 7890 123
- BIC/SWIFT: BEPAFRPPXXX
- Bank address: 12 Rue de la Banque, 75002 Paris, France

Possible correspondent/intermediary banks we see used:
- Option A (Euro rails, minimal fees): DIRECT SEPA via beneficiary IBAN (preferred for EU debit).
- Option B (USD/EUR cross-border via correspondent): CHASUS33 (JPMorgan Chase, New York) — may incur $35–$75.
- Option C (UK correspondent sometimes used): BARCGB22 (Barclays) — variable.

Payment instruction notes (choose one):
1) OUR — payer instructs their bank to pay all fees. This ensures we receive the full invoice amount. Recommended if you cannot confirm routing.
2) SHA — fees shared. Your bank will deduct routing/intermediary fees from the transfer; we will reconcile and, if the shortfall is >€100, issue a small supplemental invoice for the fee difference (we can absorb up to €100 on this invoice as a gesture).
3) NET/GROSS-UP — if you prefer to pay a grossed-up amount to ensure net receipt, we can provide a gross-up calculator (attached is a quick CSV you can populate).

Please confirm which option your Treasury prefers. If you choose SHA, let us know if you want us to accept up to €100 shortfall or require OUR to avoid any follow-up.

Also attached: wire_template-solara.csv — prefilled fields you can give to Treasury.

Confirmed: the IBAN and BIC are correct for the Paris collection account, but please use the updated BIC for correspondent messaging: BEPAFRPPXXX / CORR: CHASFRPP (we've been routed via CHAS in a handful of recent collections).

Policy guidance:
- For EU customers using SEPA (EUR to EUR IBAN) we accept SEPA (no fees).
- For non-SEPA wires (payer sending from a non-euro/overseas bank) we prefer OUR to avoid shortfalls.
- For longstanding customers where commercial relationship warrants flexibility, finance can absorb up to €100 of intermediary deductions on a case-by-case basis. Anything above €100 should be recovered via a supplemental invoice.
